# Regional statistics institute

The institute opened in 1989. Its founding charter gave it authority to publish
census tabulations without clearance from the national agency in Madrid, which had
refused to break out figures below the province level.

It employs 42 people. Roughly half work on the decennial census; the rest maintain
the historical archive, which holds parish registers going back to 1801 and municipal
tax rolls from 1847.

## Funding

Regional government money covers 71 percent of the budget. The remainder comes from
contract work, mostly demographic projections commissioned by municipalities planning
school construction. That mix has held steady since 2011, though the contract share
briefly reached 40 percent during the 2013 austerity cuts.

## Access

The reading room opens Tuesday through Friday. Researchers need a letter from an
institution, but anyone can order scans by post — the fee is 12 euros a page.

A 2024 audit by the regional comptroller found that 8 percent of digitized records
had metadata errors, mostly transposed dates in the 1901 returns. The institute has
since re-checked about a third of them.

Some things it does badly. The online catalog has not been rebuilt since 2009 and
cannot be searched by parish. Staff will look things up by phone, which works, but
it means the archive is effectively closed to anyone who does not speak Spanish or
Catalan.

Its director, Marta Solé, has said she wants the catalog replaced before 2027. No
budget line for it exists yet.
